courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

cues.en: Welcome to Data Structures and Algorithms course in JavaScript.
My name is Elshad.
I'm excited to take you on an interactive journey to master one of the most fundamental skills in computer
science.
Whether you are a self-taught developer, a computer science student, or preparing for technical interviews
at companies like Amazon, Google, meta, or Netflix.
Learning data structures and algorithms is one of the best ways to become a better problem solver and
a stronger engineer, but let's be honest.
Learning data structures and algorithms can be tough.
Many courses and books overwhelm you with theoretical explanations, walls of code, and long whiteboard
sessions that just do not stick.
Others might use the visualizations, but they only cover the simple data structures like arrays, stack
queues, and linked lists.
When it comes to the more complex structures like graph.
Graph algorithms, various types of trees, and advanced algorithms, they leave you to figure out on
your own.
And that's where this course is different.
Over the years, I've had the privilege of teaching hundreds of thousands of students data structures
and algorithms through your feedback, reviews, and requests.
I have designed this course to be truly unique, one that simplifies the even most complex topics while
keeping it engaging and practical.
We go beyond just explaining the concepts we bring them to life using powerful animations, step by
step breakdowns that make even the most challenging topics easy to understand.
Imagine trying to work with graphs.
Without the right visual understanding, it's hard to see how new nodes and edges interact, but here
you will actually see it happen.
For example, let's say we want to add a new city to a network of roads.
Before the change, maybe we only had two cities, A and B, connected by a road.
Now we introduce a new CTC and connect it to A and B instead of just looking at the code or abstract
explanations, you will watch how the graph dynamically update as each connection is formed.
Make it crystal clear how data structures work under the hood.
And we don't stop here.
Every time we introduce a data structure or an algorithm, we break it down step by step.
You will see exactly how data moves, how operations are performed, and what's happening at each stage.
Then we dive into the big O complexity analysis so you not only understand how implement a solution,
but also how efficient it is.
After each section, we have coding exercises from LeetCode and Hackerrank that reinforce your knowledge,
ensuring it stays with you forever and prepares you for interviews.
By the end of this course, you will have a strong understanding of most important data structures and
algorithms used in coding, interviews and real world application.
You will master four different types of linked lists stacks, queues, hash tables, and various types
of trees, including.
Binary tree.
Binary search tree, AVL tree heaps and trees, along with graphs and their powerful applications.
But that's just the beginning.
You will dive into most critical algorithms, from sorting and searching to recursion.
Graph traversal like breadth first search and depth first search and topological sorting, you will
conquer advanced algorithms like Dijkstra's algorithm, Bellman-ford algorithm, Floyd-warshall algorithm,
disjoint sets, Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, while also mastering grid algorithms, divide and
conquer strategies, and dynamic programming, all essential for coding interviews and real world problem
solving.
So if you are ready to finally master data structures and algorithms in a way that makes sense without
struggling through the dry explanation or getting lost in complex code, I invite you to join me in
this course.
Let's make data structures and algorithms simple, visual, and practical.
See you inside.
